chapter: Trent's band: Texas, St. Louis and the road east
title: Riverboat personnel: Stuff, Swazey, Pillars, Holloway and Jeter
summary: Who was in the band by St. Louis; Holloway's nice tone and Jeter's style as a first-chair man.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: You got Stuff where, in Ohio?
We got him in Ohio; right.
Was Haymen and (inaudible) in the band by this time? Yeah, yeah, because Jeter was in the band--Jeter was in the band already and Hayes Pillars was in the band at this time too?
By the time we got to St. Louis Hayes Pillars was in the band.
Haymen and Hollaway--Hollaway stayed in Texas; didn't he? Did he get fired from the band or what?
I don't remember how he went out.
He was a pretty good musician, but I don't think Hollaway was on the par of most of the other guys. He always did have a nice tone.
He had a nice tone and that was one of the things that kept him in the band as long as he did.
How was Jeter as a player?
Jeter was more of a guy--
He wasn't a get-off man really?
He was a first man mostly.
